memories.summary: Mia began the year in Honolulu, leading a coral reef survey to assess bleaching after an unusually warm season. Her team documented temperature data and collected coral samples for genetic resilience studies.
memories.what: Conducting coral reef health assessments and data collection.

memories.summary: In Sydney, Mia collaborated with local divers to tag sea turtles for migration tracking. She spent several days diving off the Great Barrier Reef, carefully attaching transmitters and noting behavioral patterns.
memories.what: Tagging and tracking sea turtles in the Great Barrier Reef.

memories.summary: Mia traveled to Bali to host a marine conservation workshop for students. She explained how coastal waste impacts coral ecosystems and demonstrated hands-on methods for monitoring microplastic accumulation.
memories.what: Teaching a workshop on microplastic pollution and coral protection.

memories.summary: In Cape Town, Mia joined a research expedition studying penguin population decline. She worked alongside ecologists to collect blood samples and measure chick growth rates over a two-week period.
memories.what: Participating in a penguin population monitoring expedition.

memories.summary: While visiting Lisbon, Mia attended an international ocean policy summit. She delivered a talk on community-led marine restoration and emphasized the need for localized solutions in global conservation efforts.
memories.what: Presenting at a global ocean conservation conference.

memories.summary: During her fieldwork in Okinawa, Mia conducted nighttime dives to observe bioluminescent plankton behavior. She captured high-resolution images later used for a public science exhibition in Japan.
memories.what: Documenting bioluminescent plankton through underwater photography.

memories.summary: Mia spent several weeks in Vancouver collaborating with a local nonprofit to rehabilitate stranded seals. She assisted in medical care, feeding schedules, and public education about marine rescue operations.
memories.what: Rehabilitating stranded seals and supporting marine animal care.

memories.summary: In San Diego, Mia taught a summer course on oceanography, combining classroom lectures with beachside experiments. She encouraged students to collect sand samples and measure salinity changes across tides.
memories.what: Teaching field-based lessons on oceanography and marine chemistry.

memories.summary: Mia returned to Tokyo to work with colleagues on a paper analyzing deep-sea sonar data. The team discovered previously undocumented coral formations at depths exceeding 2,000 meters.
memories.what: Researching deep-sea coral structures through sonar analysis.

memories.summary: To conclude the year, Mia presented her findings at a UN ocean science forum in Geneva. She highlighted how cross-border collaboration can accelerate ocean restoration and shared visual footage from her global dives.
memories.what: Presenting global marine research outcomes at an international forum.
